summary: ql-9's 'capped/SAMPLED' honesty fix was applied only to athena-hunter's total_rows, but the fields the sweep-4 doc literally names ('total_alerts/flows/dns') live in alert-triage — and they are still uncapped len() of LIMIT-bounded queries presented to the LLM and UI as true totals.
code:
"total_alerts": len(enriched_alerts),
"total_flows": len(conn_flows),   # conn_flows fetched with LIMIT 100
"total_dns": len(dns_logs),        # dns_logs fetched with LIMIT 50
# ...no 'capped'/'sampled' flag anywhere; triage_data JSON dumped verbatim into llm_triage user_content
scenario: A busy window has 5,000 conn flows. athena_conn is called with limit=100 -> conn_flows has exactly 100 rows -> total_flows=100 is put into triage_data and returned in data.total_flows. The LLM (told nothing about the cap) states '100 flows' as a complete count, and the UI renders total_flows:100 as fact. This is the identical 'counts of LIMIT-capped result sets presented as true totals' bug ql-9 claimed to fix; ql-9's own test only exercised athena-hunter's total_rows, so this sibling instance in the agent that actually owns the total_alerts/flows/dns names was never touched.
suggested_fix: Mirror ql-9 in alert-triage: track whether any source query returned exactly its LIMIT (e.g. len(suricata_alerts)>=100, len(conn_flows)>=100, len(dns_logs)>=50) and add a 'counts_sampled': true flag + '(at least N, sampled)' labeling into triage_data before it reaches the LLM, and surface it in the returned data block.

summary: cc-1's kill-switch fails OPEN on EVERY error path, so the emergency feed-freeze is silently defeated by a single transient orchestrator poll failure (timeout, 5xx, momentary DNS/connection blip) for up to one full KILL_POLL_MS window, resuming the broadcast of real Athena alerts during an active kill.
scenario: Operator hits the emergency kill because sensitive alerts are showing on the demo projector. athenaKilled becomes true on the next 15s poll. Then the orchestrator has one slow/aborted response (AbortSignal.timeout at 10s, or a transient 503) — the catch/non-200 branch sets athenaKilled=false, and the trickle timer resumes dequeuing and broadcasting real restricted alerts to every connected client until a later poll re-confirms the kill. The freeze is only as reliable as an unbroken poll stream, and it fails toward leaking rather than toward safe. The direct questions checked out (fail-safe holds on all paths; athenaKilled can never get STUCK true) — this is the honest flip side: it can get un-stuck at the worst moment. Documented as intended in sweep 4, but the emergency security control is not reliable under orchestrator flakiness.
suggested_fix: Distinguish 'confirmed not-killed' (a 200 with athena_hunter=false) from 'could not determine' (timeout/5xx/parse error). On an indeterminate result, RETAIN the last known athenaKilled state (or fail toward frozen once a kill has been observed) rather than unconditionally clearing to false; only a successful 200 should be allowed to lift an active freeze.

summary: ql-7 (unknown severity -> visible 'unknown' bucket, not buried as 'low') and ql-8 (canonical numeric mapping) were extended to athena-hunter only for the 1/2/3 cases. For unparseable/blank/numeric-4+ severities, athena-hunter's feed normalizer still collapses to 'low', diverging from alert-triage._norm_sev which yields 'unknown' — the same event carries different labels across the feed and triage surfaces, and genuinely-unknown alerts stay buried at the bottom of the feed (the exact defect ql-7 set out to kill).
code:
# athena-hunter _normalize_severity:
return {1: "high", 2: "medium", 3: "low"}.get(n, "low")   # 4+/unknown -> low
# ...else fall-throughs also -> "low"
# alert-triage _norm_sev: same 1/2/3, but unrecognized -> "unknown"
scenario: A Suricata alert with alert_severity '4' (or a NULL/garbage severity) arrives on the live feed via /alerts/recent. athena-hunter labels it 'low' (sorts to the bottom, visually deprioritized), while the same row through alert-triage is labeled 'unknown' and kept visible. ql-8's stated goal ('so the same event isn't labeled differently across surfaces') and ql-7's goal ('unknown must not be hidden as low') are both only half-met. Note this is partly forced by the shared Alert TS type only permitting critical|high|medium|low|informational (no 'unknown'), so a full fix needs the type widened or a distinct visible treatment.
suggested_fix: Either widen the Alert.severity union (and feed rendering) to include 'unknown' and map athena-hunter's out-of-range/unparseable cases to it, or explicitly document that the feed intentionally floors unknowns to 'low' and accept the cross-surface divergence. At minimum keep 4+/blank from silently reading as a benign 'low' if the feed drives any prioritization.
